text:
lara: FYI CI started failing for the quantized-model bring-up. eval-runner jobs produce zero-length trace blobs — uploader returns 200 but dashboard shows no traces. Happened on 3 runs (2026-03-19). Anyone else seeing this?
aj: Saw the same. Quick reproducer: run eval-runner with --chunked-gzip and small batch size. Uploader logs show `200 OK` but `content-length: 0`. S3 shows multipart objects where the manifest exists but parts missing or flagged as 0 bytes.
mio: I dug into trace-writer. When chunking+gzip is enabled we set `Content-Encoding: gzip` per chunk but we forgot to include `X-Trace-Version` on each chunk. trace-summarizer currently filters chunks/manifests by that header and silently drops anything without it — server accepted the upload but summarizer ignored it -> manifests with no valid parts -> effectively empty traces in the dashboard.
kevin: FWIW I also noticed an old lifecycle rule applied to `eval-traces/experimental/` — there are delete markers from 2025-11-02. That explains some historical gaps but not the new zero-byte uploads.
ci-bot: build #1456: eval-harness/trace-summarizer timed out after 10m — failing test: `trace-integration`.
lara: Proposed fixes: (1) make uploader include `X-Trace-Version: trace-v3` on every chunk and on the manifest metadata. (2) make summarizer fall back to sniffing gzip magic bytes if header is missing (backcompat). (3) uploader should emit `X-Chunk-Checksum` + `Content-Length` per chunk and log the chunk UUID so we can trace missing parts. (4) add CI job that runs eval-runner with chunked-gzip enabled and asserts manifest completeness.
aj: +1. Also: make manifest writes idempotent (manifest UUID + conditional put) — current retries sometimes create duplicate manifests and summarizer dedup logic is brittle.
mio: I'll open a PR for summarizer fallback + the CI test and add a small unit test for header-less blobs. I'll also add parsing of gzip magic as a fallback. Need uploader to add header so tests hit real mix.
kevin: Retention proposal (initial): raw per-sample traces (full payloads) -> 120 days. Aggregated/flattened metrics and eval-summaries -> 730 days. Manifests/indexes -> 365 days. Sampled debug traces (<=1MB) -> 540 days. Also: exempt `eval-traces/experimental/` from aggressive lifecycle or move experimental to a different bucket to avoid accidental GC.
lara: Owners for rollout: mio -> summarizer changes + tests, aj -> uploader changes + canary, kevin -> infra/lifecycle and S3 inventory. Canary plan: uploader header change canary to prod for 24h (low %), summarizer fallback behind a feature flag for 48h, then enable globally. Add nightly CI job `eval-trace-chunked` to run the chunked path.
aj: I'll implement uploader header+checksum and add per-chunk logging (example):
```
headers = {
  'Content-Encoding': 'gzip',
  'X-Trace-Version': 'trace-v3',
  'X-Chunk-Checksum': sha256_hex(chunk)
}
# multipart upload: include chunk_uuid in manifest entry
```
Question: do we attempt to reprocess traces where summarizer dropped parts in last 7 days? Might be useful if parts still exist.
mio: We can reprocess manifests for the last 7 days as a batch job if parts are still present in S3. The summarizer can be run in a 'reindex' mode that accepts missing headers and will try to reconstruct. We'll need a safe-run flag and small parallelism to avoid hammering S3.
kevin: I'll run S3 inventory and check if parts still exist. If lifecycle already removed them, reprocessing won't help. I'll post the inventory results by tomorrow EOD.
lara: Action items: aj => open uploader PR and schedule canary; mio => open summarizer PR + add CI test; kevin => run S3 inventory, update lifecycle rule, and coordinate bucket moves for `experimental/`. ci-bot => add nightly `eval-trace-chunked` job (can someone file infra ticket?). Reconvene tomorrow 10am PT. Thanks all. :thumbsup: :hourglass:
